title: Bail conditions that get violated most often
p1:
Getting bail does not mean the case is over. One small mistake after release can bring someone back behind bars.

Many people think bail violations only happen when someone commits another crime. The reality is often very different.
p2:
Some of the most common violations are surprisingly simple: missing a court date, failing to report to authorities when required, contacting a person the court has ordered them to avoid, or leaving an area without permission.

A condition that looks minor on paper can have serious consequences.
p3:
Bail conditions are not punishments before trial. They are rules designed to make sure the person returns to court and does not interfere with the legal process.

The biggest takeaway: read every bail condition carefully and treat it like a legal responsibility, not a suggestion. A misunderstanding is not always a defence for a violation.
